{{Short description|American chemist and Quaker (1922–2022)}}

{{Use mdy dates|date=September 2021}}
'''Edward McCollin Arnett''' (September 25, 1922 – May 11, 2022) was an American chemist.<ref>{{cite book |title=Who's who in the South and Southwest |date=1984 |publisher=Marquis Who's Who |page=25 }}</ref>

==Early life==
Born in [[Philadelphia]], to John Hancock Arnett, a physician, and Katherine Williams McCollin,<ref name="The New York Times 1985">{{cite web | title=JOHN HANCOCK ARNETT | website=The New York Times | date=1985-11-22 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1985/11/22/us/john-hancock-arnett.html | access-date=2021-09-16}}</ref> a singer and composer, Arnett was a Quaker and [[conscientious objector]] who served in the [[Civilian Public Service]] during World War II.{{sfn |Arnett |2012 |p=}}{{page needed|date=September 2021}} Arnett completed his undergraduate degree at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], and in 1949, earned a Ph.D. from the same institution.<ref>{{cite news|title=Edward M. Arnett|url=https://chem.duke.edu/faculty/edward-m-arnett|accessdate=23 March 2018|publisher=Duke University|archive-date=April 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160405073921/http://chem.duke.edu/faculty/edward-m-arnett|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Academic career==
He began teaching at the [[University of Pittsburgh]] in 1957.{{sfn |Arnett |2012 |p=}}{{page needed|date=September 2021}} In 1968, Arnett was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]].<ref name="gugg">{{cite news|title=Edward M. Arnett|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/edward-m-arnett/|accessdate=23 March 2018|publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation}}</ref>  He joined the faculty of [[Duke University]] in 1980 and, three years later, was named a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="gugg"/> At Duke, Arnett was appointed the R.J. Reynolds Professor of Chemistry, and retired in 1992.<ref>{{cite news|title=Edward M. Arnett|url=https://scholars.duke.edu/person/edward.arnett|accessdate=23 March 2018|publisher=Duke University|archive-date=February 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190201200132/https://scholars.duke.edu/person/edward.arnett|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Arnett died on May 11, 2022, at the age of 99.<ref>{{cite web |title=Edward Arnett |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/heraldsun/name/edward-arnett-obituary?pid=202017939 |website=Legacy |access-date=18 May 2022 |date=18 May 2022}}</ref>
